stem:
Meera heats some sugar in a dry test tube in her school laboratory. She observes that a black solid is left behind and droplets of water collect on the cooler parts of the tube.

What does this experiment show about sugar?

options.text: Sugar is an element because it leaves behind only one black solid.
Sugar is a compound because it breaks down on heating to give carbon and water, showing it contains more than one element.
Sugar is a mixture because it gives two different products on heating.
Sugar is an element because the water droplets come from the sugar, not from the air.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating sugar decomposes it into carbon (black solid) and water; since water contains hydrogen and oxygen, sugar must contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, so it is a compound. A is the trap for a student who ignores the water product and judges only from the single black solid; D misuses the decomposition evidence; C confuses compound with mixture.
